source.title: Reducing Overestimation Bias by Increasing Representation Dissimilarity in Ensemble Based Deep Q-Learning

record.file_problem: none noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures similarity between Q-network representations with linear-kernel CKA and relates it to ensemble performance, rather than testing convergence with model scale.
record.gate_note: The study reports CKA comparisons of network representations. Downstream reward curves are not rows because they measure task performance, not representation similarity. The t-SNE visualizations are not recorded as pairwise similarity outcomes; the text describes them qualitatively but does not give a pairwise similarity measure.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (deep Q-learning ensembles), the study measures linear CKA between same-architecture Q-networks with different initializations. That bears on V3, which says seeds converge on shared representations. The networks are not independently trained: they share a replay buffer and a coupled Maxmin or averaged target. That shared target partly forces agreement, especially at the output layer, so this is a weak, indirect test.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors claim ensemble Q-networks often converge to a common representation and that this high similarity causes, not merely accompanies, worse performance. They show that five inequality or consensus regularizers on parameter L2 norms significantly improve MaxminDQN and EnsembleDQN, including under identical initialization.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies linear-kernel CKA to Q-function ensembles and introduces diversity regularization; it does not reproduce the original sources' convergence methods or test convergence with scale.
record.method_sensitivity: Observed CKA similarity varied across training snapshots; regularized and baseline networks also differed in reported output-layer similarity.

fits_no_version.finding: Fully connected networks of 64 and 32 hidden units, trained on sine regression with different seeds, batches and learning rates, reach high corresponding-layer CKA and 98% output similarity after training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Networks of different widths trained on the same simple task converge to similar layerwise representations.

fits_no_version.finding: Higher CKA between ensemble Q-networks coincides with lower return. Diversity regularization on parameter norms lowers output-layer CKA to about 90% and improves return.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation convergence among ensemble members harms ensemble RL performance.

record.problems: The direct representation-similarity results are mostly described qualitatively or as approximate aggregates. The study uses one representation-similarity measure, linear-kernel CKA, and does not test scaling or broad cross-architecture, cross-objective, or cross-modal alignment.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted due to the 60-row limit. The t-SNE figures and training-return results were left out because they do not report pairwise representation similarity.

untested.parts: Whether individual units or bases match versus only shared subspaces. Convergence under fully independent training with no shared targets or buffer.
No scale or capability sweep and no cross-architecture or cross-objective comparison.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation test.
No interpretable feature or circuit comparison.
Only linear CKA is used. No metric, setting or input-distribution comparison.
No plateau analysis or attribution to shared data or objectives, although shared targets are a plausible cause that goes untested.

missing.what: Per-environment and per-algorithm corresponding-layer CKA diagonals for baseline two-network ensembles; the record only gives the authors' output-layer summary.

record.verdict_notes: V3 evidence is indirect: the ensemble members are trained jointly with shared targets, not independently, and the headline number is output-layer CKA, which a shared target nearly forces. The similarity-performance link rests on four snapshots from one run. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size or capability, and no test of whether cross-model alignment rises with scale.
No vision-language model comparison or paired image-caption representations.
The study measures representation similarity between Q-functions, but does not identify shared individual features or test whether units or bases match.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment test.
No test of recurring interpretable features, neurons, or circuits.
The study uses linear-kernel CKA but does not compare similarity metrics, their settings, or input distributions.
The study does not test whether alignment plateaus or whether shared data or objectives explain it rather than a common model of reality.

rows.subject: Two-network MaxminDQN and EnsembleDQN experiments
rows.stage_stated: after training; averaged over five seeds
rows.operation_detail: Measured corresponding-layer similarity with linear-kernel CKA
rows.measure: CKA similarity at the output layer
rows.value: More than 96% similarity in almost all scenarios.
rows.note: This is the authors' summary across the plotted two-network experiments, not a separate value for each algorithm and environment.
rows.check: The value is output-layer CKA under a shared or coupled target, which inflates agreement. Figure 7 also gives per-layer diagonals by environment and algorithm that the row does not record.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix C.3, opening paragraph and Figure 7: linear-kernel CKA after training, averaged over five seeds; baseline output-layer similarity exceeds 96% in almost all scenarios.

rows.subject: Two-network regularized MaxminDQN and EnsembleDQN experiments
rows.stage_stated: after training; averaged over five seeds
rows.operation_detail: Measured corresponding-layer similarity with linear-kernel CKA
rows.measure: CKA similarity at the output layer
rows.baseline: Baseline output-layer similarity was more than 96% in almost all scenarios.
rows.note: The paper reports this as an approximate aggregate for regularized versions, without separate values by regularizer, algorithm, or environment.
rows.check: A regularizer built to push the networks apart is a deliberate intervention. The reduced similarity (about 90%) is the method's own effect, not convergence arising naturally, so this should not inform V3.

relationships.condition: Baseline (unregularized) two-network MaxminDQN and EnsembleDQN, after training (Catcher, PixelCopter, Asterix), and Catcher MaxminDQN at episodes 1000 and 3000
relationships.reason: Different-seed same-architecture Q-networks reach very high CKA: over 96% at the output in almost all baseline runs, and described as extremely high across layers at B and D (R4, R6, R7). The networks share a coupled target, however.
relationships.display_finding: Output CKA exceeded 96% in almost all baseline runs, with very high similarity also observed across layers; the networks shared a coupled target.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v3 dated January 2022, titled Preventing Value Function Collapse in Ensemble Q-Learning by Maximizing Representation Diversity, differing from the pack's title/year. Shared replay and coupled targets limit generalization to independently trained models; the study does not isolate how much coupling increases agreement.
